newsitem.title: USA: Armey does not expect U.S. budget deal this week.
newsitem.headline: Armey does not expect U.S. budget deal this week.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey said he did not expect Republicans and White House negotiators to reach a balanced budget deal this week, but did not entirely rule an accord out.
At a news conference, the Texas Republican also said he would not accept a political fix of the Consumer Price Index, saying that job should be left to Labor Department experts.

"I don't rule that out (budget deal) but I'm not expecting it," Armey said. He emphasized once again that congressional Republicans would bring their own budget plan to a vote in early May with or without a deal.

"There will be no, as it were, political agreement on what would be the CPI," Armey said. He said that if the Labor Department adjusted the inflation measure "and announced it to the world, we would accept" that.

Armey said he expected any budget legislation crafted by Republicans to build on progress that has been made during weeks of private negotiations between the White House and Republicans. He also said that a budget package could be divided into separate bills, with Medicare a high priority.
Armey said by the end of the year the White House and Congress would accomplish the budget task they set out to do.
Armey said Republicans would not do anything in a budget bill that would be "offensive to the goodwill" that has been built up during budget negotiations.
Armey basically outlined a budget process where negotiations continued with the White House during coming months as Republicans brought up their own budget, tax, Medicare and spending bills.
He refused to say whether Republicans would push spending cuts before a tax-cutting bill.
